en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Pregnant Women, 70.
The Second Training Rule on Co-residents.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the nun Thullanandā, having given the full admission to a co-resident female disciple, neither sent her away nor had her sent away.
Her husband seized her.
Those nuns who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, complained, and spread it about, saying:
“How can it be that the noble lady Thullanandā, having ordained a co-resident nun, neither sends her away herself nor causes her to be sent away, even though her husband has seized her?
If this nun had departed, her husband would not have seized her. … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā, having ordained a co-resident nun, neither sends her away herself nor causes her to be sent away, even though her husband has seized her?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:

“… How can this happen, monks? How indeed could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given the full admission to her co-resident, neither have her leave nor cause her to leave, even though her husband has taken her?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:

‘If a nun, having given the full admission to a co-resident, neither sends her away nor causes her to be sent away, even for as little as five or six yojanas, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But which [nun]" means whichever such [nun]... "a nun" means... [as before].
... [as before] ... this is the nun intended in this context.
A "co-resident" (sahajīvinī) is said to be a student (saddhivihārinī).
"Having caused to emerge" means having conferred full ordination (*upasampadā*).
"Nor should she cause her to withdraw" means...
One should not go away oneself;
"one should not cause another to go away" means one should not command another.
“I will neither cause [the meal] to be interrupted nor cause it to be interrupted even for as little as five or six yojanas”— if one merely abandons this resolve, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
There is no offense if there is an obstacle.
If she has searched for a companion nun but does not find one,
or if she is ill,
or in times of distress.
"Of one who is insane," "of one who is a first-offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The Seventh Chapter on Pregnant Women.
